issues.description: The milk method signature for milking an animal is inconsistent across the materials. The Problem Statement Part 2 (problem_statement.md line 93) instructs implementing messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (a method taking a double parameter), while the UML and other artifacts declare and use a parameterless method messageOnMilk(): String (UML in problem_statement.md line 52; the provided template Main calls m.messageOnMilk() at src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 31; the reference solution defines the interface as String messageOnMilk() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5 and implements it in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 19). This mismatch (parameter vs no-parameter) will either cause compilation errors or failing tests and will block students from knowing which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the milk method signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred minimal-impact fix: update the Problem Statement Part 2 to require the parameterless signature messageOnMilk(): String and change the example return text there to the no-arg form (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), matching the UML, template, and solution. Alternatively, if the teaching goal is to pass a milk volume, update the UML, template, solution interface and all implementations/call sites to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust examples/tests accordingly.
